title: Riverside footbridge: repair or replace?
question: Should the council repair the Riverside footbridge, replace it, or replace it with a wider bridge for walking and cycling?
summary: A 1974 steel footbridge is corroding. It is the only step-free crossing to a school and a row of shops. This map shows the options, what a closure would be like for the people who use the bridge, and what the council still has to decide. All names and figures are made up.

reading: Three views. The first traces the decision from what the inspection found to a bridge people can use, and whether it worked; switch between Today and Planned to see what exists and what is proposed. The second, The works, option by option, follows each option from committee to reopening across the council, designers, contractor, river authority and funders, so you can compare how long each takes and who it depends on. The third shows what a resident goes through before, during and after a closure. Turn on Show technical names to see engineering detail. Notes from the structural engineer, access, safety, finance and residents sit on the boxes they are about.

checked.note: Checked against the principal inspection, early costs, two weeks of crossing counts, an access audit, quotes for temporary crossings, the programme and suppliers, a shops survey, and one public drop-in session.

glossary.load rating: The weight a bridge can safely carry, worked out by an engineer.
glossary.bearings: The parts at each end that let the bridge move a little as it warms and cools.
glossary.section loss: Steel lost to rust, as a share of the original thickness.
glossary.shared use: A path for people walking and cycling together.
glossary.rest landing: A flat section partway up a ramp where people can stop.
glossary.fabricated steel: Steel parts cut, shaped and welded in a factory before they come to site.
glossary.framework: A list of contractors the council has already vetted and can hire without a full tender.
glossary.programme: The timetable for the works, week by week.

evidence.text: Corrosion at 6 of 14 lower joints; two show section loss over 20%.
With repairs, another 25 years is realistic. Without them, we would recommend a weight limit within three years.
Bearings at the north end have seized; the bridge cannot expand freely in summer.
Repair £1.1m, 10 weeks closed, 25 years. Replace £3.4m, 9 months closed, 100 years. Wider replacement £4.2m, 11 months, 100 years.
A regional cycling fund could pay up to 40% of a widened bridge, if bid by November.
The river authority needs 6 months' notice for any work in the water.
It's the only step-free way to the school. A long closure means a 20-minute walk round by the main road.
It's too narrow to pass anyone. If you're rebuilding, make it wider.
Last time it shut for a month, my takings dropped by a third.
The ramps at the north end are too steep for me on my own.
Estimates are ±30% at this stage.
Average 1,900 crossings a day on school days, 1,100 at weekends.
About 260 crossings in each school-time peak; cycles and prams often wait for each other.
22% of crossings are cycles.
About 40 wheelchair or mobility scooter crossings a day.
Counts in the school summer holidays were 45% lower than in term time.
Temporary step-free bridge, 2 m wide: £380k for 9 months; needs its own 6 months' river notice.
Minibus shuttle at school times: £1,450 a week, about 12 minutes each way, one wheelchair space.
The road bridge footway is 1.4 m wide; two prams cannot pass.
North ramp: 1 in 10 over 14 m with no rest landing; the standard is 1 in 15 with a landing every 10 m.
Two of six lamps on the north approach do not work; handrail on one side only.
Rebuilding the north ramp to 1 in 15 needs 7 m more length, so the ramp must turn back on itself.
Fabricated steel for a new bridge takes 20 to 24 weeks from order; repair steel and bearings 8 weeks.
Committee meets 15 September, then 10 November. Cycling fund bids close 28 November; decisions in March.
A full closure must avoid the two weeks before Christmas, when the shops are busiest.
Five of eight shops said takings fell by a quarter or more during the last four-week closure.
What would help shops most: clear signs (7 of 8), works in summer (6), a rates holiday (5), a shuttle stop (4).
Several people asked whether the old bridge could stay open while a new one is built.

gaps.title: A way across during a long closure
gaps.why: A nine-month closure without a crossing cuts off the school's only step-free route.

stories.as: As a parent with a pram, I want a step-free way across while the bridge is shut, so the school run stays under ten minutes.
done_when: a temporary crossing or shuttle runs at school times
the route is signed and lit
the detour is no more than 10 minutes longer

stories.as: As a wheelchair user, I want to be sure of a place on the shuttle, so I am not left behind at school time.
done_when: a wheelchair space can be booked by text
a second space is added at the two school-time peaks

stories.as: As the council lead, I want the cost of each way across side by side, so the committee can choose.
done_when: shuttle, temporary bridge and detour are compared on cost, time and step-free access
the comparison is in the 15 September report

gaps.title: Ramps people can use on their own
gaps.why: The north ramp is 1 in 10 with no landing; the standard is 1 in 15.

stories.as: As a wheelchair user, I want ramps I can manage alone, so I do not need help to cross.
done_when: ramp slopes meet the access standard
a wheelchair user tests the design before it is approved

stories.as: As a parent with a pram, I want a rest landing on the way up, so I can stop safely.
done_when: a level landing at least every 10 m
handrails on both sides

gaps.title: Bid to the cycling fund by November
gaps.why: Up to 40% of a wider bridge could be paid for, but only with a bid by 28 November.

stories.as: As finance, I want a fall-back if the bid fails, so we are not stuck in March.

gaps.title: Weekly news during works

stories.as: As a shop owner, I want to know a week ahead if the end date moves, so I can plan stock and staff.

notes.title: Repairs buy 25 years, not 100
notes.body: Repair is sound engineering, but the bridge will need replacing in the 2050s anyway.
notes.recommend: Compare options over 50 years, not on build cost alone.
notes.question: Do we judge the options over 50 years of cost and closures?

notes.title: The river notice sets the earliest start
notes.body: Any option needs six months' notice for work in the water.
notes.recommend: Send a notice for the larger option now; it can be narrowed later.
notes.question: Can we give notice before the committee decides?

notes.title: Seized bearings are a summer risk
notes.body: A bridge that cannot expand is stressed on hot days.
notes.recommend: Free or replace the north bearings this year, whatever we decide.
notes.question: Do we fix the bearings now as urgent work?

notes.title: The school run is the hardest hit
notes.body: Families with prams have no other step-free route.
notes.recommend: Plan the closure around school holidays where possible.
notes.question: Can the longest part of the works fall in the summer holidays?

notes.title: Shops felt the last closure
notes.body: One owner lost a third of takings during a one-month closure.
notes.recommend: Talk to the south-side shops before setting dates; consider signs that say 'shops open'.
notes.question: Is there any support we can offer shops during a long closure?

notes.title: Fix the ramps in either option
notes.body: A repair could rebuild the north ramps too.
notes.recommend: Include gentler ramps in the repair option so the comparison is fair.
notes.question: Does the repair price include new ramps?

notes.title: The fund changes the sums
notes.body: With 40% from the fund, the wider bridge costs the council about £2.5m.
notes.recommend: Show the committee both prices: with and without the fund.
notes.question: Do we commit to the wider option if the bid fails?

notes.title: The estimates are rough
notes.body: At ±30%, repair and replace overlap less than they seem, but the ranking could still shift.
notes.recommend: Show ranges, not single numbers.
notes.question: Do we wait for firmer prices before deciding?

notes.title: Say what we are aiming for
notes.body: Residents care about the closure as much as the bridge.
notes.recommend: State the aim as a safe crossing with the shortest closure we can manage.
notes.question: Which matters more to the committee: lowest cost or shortest closure?

notes.title: An assistant can draft the weekly update
notes.body: Site photos and the contractor's diary hold most of the news.
notes.recommend: Let an assistant draft the Friday update from the diary; a council officer approves it.
notes.question: Who approves the weekly update before it goes out?

notes.title: Wider means safer, not just nicer
notes.body: People cannot pass on the current width.
notes.recommend: Treat 4 m as the access option, not an extra.
notes.question: Is 4 m enough for the expected number of cycles?

notes.title: Steel lead time decides the closure start
notes.body: Fabricated steel takes 20 to 24 weeks; nothing can close until it is near delivery.
notes.recommend: Plan the closure back from the steel delivery date, not forward from the decision.
notes.question: Can we place a provisional steel order before the fund decision?

notes.title: A new north ramp changes the repair
notes.body: Reaching 1 in 15 means a longer ramp that turns back on itself.
notes.recommend: Price the repair with and without a new north ramp.
notes.question: Do we compare repair-with-ramp against replacement, not bare repair?

notes.title: Check the bearings in the first hot week
notes.body: Freeing the bearings fixes the summer risk only if they move as expected.
notes.recommend: Measure movement on the first day over 25°C.
notes.question: Who takes the reading and where is it recorded?

notes.title: The fund decision lands in March
notes.body: Choosing the wider option in September means waiting five months to know if it is affordable.
notes.recommend: Agree the fall-back in September so March is not a new decision.
notes.question: What is the fall-back if the bid is refused: repair, or replace at today's width?

notes.title: Agree the measures before the works
notes.body: Counts already exist, so we can compare like with like.
notes.recommend: Keep the counter in place through and after the works.
notes.question: Do we judge success on crossings in term time only?

notes.title: Whole-life cost and closure months, side by side
notes.body: Repair is cheapest now but returns in 25 years with another closure.
notes.recommend: Show cost over 50 years and total months closed for each option.
notes.question: Which weighs more for us: total cost over 50 years, or months closed?

notes.title: A way across is part of the option, not an extra
notes.body: A long closure without one cuts off the school's step-free route.
notes.recommend: Price each replacement option with its way across included.
notes.question: Do we rule out any option that has no step-free way across?

notes.title: The detour is not safe for prams at peak
notes.body: The road bridge footway is 1.4 m; two prams cannot pass, and the detour crosses a busy road twice.
notes.recommend: Add a crossing patrol at school times if the detour is used.
notes.question: Can we staff a crossing patrol for the whole closure?

notes.title: Fix the lamps before anything else
notes.body: Broken lamps on the north approach make it feel unsafe after dark.
notes.recommend: Fix within a month as routine maintenance.
notes.question: Who owns the lamp repair, highways or lighting?

notes.title: The lift needs a weekend road closure
notes.body: Lifting the old and new spans needs a crane and a road closure.
notes.recommend: Book the lift weekend early and tell bus operators.
notes.question: Which weekend avoids school and Christmas trading?

notes.title: One wheelchair space is not enough at peak
notes.body: About 40 wheelchair or scooter crossings a day; the shuttle has one space per trip.
notes.recommend: Add a second accessible vehicle at the two school-time peaks.
notes.question: Will we guarantee a space for wheelchair users at school times?

notes.title: People asked for room to pass
notes.body: Cycles and prams wait for each other at peak; a cyclist asked for a wider bridge.
notes.recommend: Use the counts and comments in the fund bid.
notes.question: Do we ask the drop-in group to back the bid?

notes.title: Could the old bridge stay open?
notes.body: Several people asked if the old bridge could stay open while a new one is built.
notes.recommend: Ask the design team whether a new bridge beside the old one is possible.
notes.question: Is building beside the old bridge worth a quick study?

notes.title: Signs should name the shops
notes.body: Shops' top request was clear signs.
notes.recommend: Put shop names and walking times on the detour signs.
notes.question: Can the shops supply their own sign board at the bridge ends?

notes.title: Test the new ramp with the people who use it
notes.body: A wheelchair user said they cannot manage the north ramp alone.
notes.recommend: Invite two wheelchair users to test the ramp before it opens.
notes.question: Who invites the testers and records what they find?

notes.title: Repair returns the question in 25 years
notes.body: £1.1m now, plus a likely replacement around 2050.
notes.recommend: Show the second closure and its cost in the repair option.
notes.question: Do we include a 2050 replacement in the repair option's cost?

notes.title: A temporary bridge costs a third of a repair
notes.body: £380k for nine months against a shuttle at about £56k.
notes.recommend: Compare the shuttle with the temporary bridge per crossing.
notes.question: Is the temporary bridge worth £380k for nine months?

notes.title: An agent can sort complaints and answer the routine ones
notes.body: Most questions will be dates and detours.
notes.recommend: Let an agent answer routine questions from the latest update; people handle the rest.
notes.question: Which complaints must always go to a person?

notes.title: An agent can assemble the fund bid
notes.body: The bid needs counts, comments and costs already in this canvas.
notes.recommend: Draft the bid from the canvas evidence for officers to edit.
notes.question: Who signs off the bid before it goes in?

notes.title: Shops want summer works
notes.body: Six of eight shops said summer works would help most; term-time counts are 45% higher.
notes.recommend: Aim the longest closure at the summer holidays.
notes.question: Can a nine-month closure start in July so the worst comes in summer?

notes.title: The bearings are already decided
notes.body: Freeing the bearings goes ahead in August whatever the committee chooses.
notes.recommend: Say so in the report so it is not reopened.
notes.question: Do we report the bearing work as done before 15 September?

decisions.decision: Yes. Bearings freed in August as urgent works.
